gen_risks.description: Target private capital mobilization of US$150 million may not be achieved, limiting the fund’s impact on startups and job creation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Expand outreach to additional regional and international VC funds, set quarterly mobilization targets, and activate a rapid‑response pipeline to attract new investors when shortfalls appear.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 20 – PDO expects US$150 million private capital mobilized.

gen_risks.description: Concentration of investments in a single VC fund could expose the ISSF to high loss if that fund underperforms.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce updated concentration limits (no more than 15 % of total loan per fund), regularly monitor exposure, and diversify across multiple funds and stages.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 34 – Concentration risk management caps at US$5 million / 30 % ownership.

gen_risks.description: Turnover of key ISSF staff or board members could disrupt project implementation and governance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement retention contracts, succession planning, and a formal nomination process to ensure timely replacement of board members.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 41 – Lessons learned on high turnover and need for stable team.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient operational due diligence (ODD) on underlying VC funds may allow fraud, mismanagement, or regulatory breaches.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate a robust ODD framework, conduct periodic third‑party audits of VC funds, and train ISSF staff on ODD best practices.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 41 – ODD will be integrated to assess compliance and governance.

gen_risks.description: Climate‑related extreme events could disrupt startup operations, especially those not focused on greentech.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prioritize investments in greentech and climate‑resilient solutions; include climate risk assessment in investment screening.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 12 – Climate vulnerability noted but deemed low impact.

gen_risks.description: Improper e‑waste handling by ICT‑focused SMEs could cause pollution and health hazards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Require funded startups to adopt certified e‑waste recycling plans and embed ESG clauses in investment agreements.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 77 – Potential environmental impacts from e‑waste mismanagement.

gen_risks.description: Startups may face data‑privacy and cybersecurity breaches, harming users and reputations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mandate compliance with international data‑protection standards (e.g., GDPR/ISO 27001) and provide cybersecurity capacity‑building grants.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 78 – Risks include data privacy and security concerns.

gen_risks.description: A regional or global downturn in venture‑capital markets could reduce follow‑on funding and returns.
gen_risks.mitigation: Diversify investments across stages, sectors, and geographies; maintain a reserve fund to support portfolio companies during market stress.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 59 – Acknowledgement of global VC downturn but portfolio performance remains promising.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient successful exits may limit the fund’s financial returns and ability to recycle capital.
gen_risks.mitigation: Select startups with clear exit pathways, engage strategic corporate investors early, and allocate follow‑on capital to accelerate growth.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 14 – Only two exits to date; expectation of more in coming years.

gen_risks.description: Regulatory changes in the fintech sandbox or other sectors could render invested business models non‑compliant.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain continuous liaison with MODEE and other regulators; embed regulatory compliance checks in due‑diligence.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 25 – Fintech Regulatory Sandbox re‑launched with growing demand.

gen_risks.description: The project may fail to meet its gender‑inclusion targets, reducing impact on women’s economic participation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a Gender Action Plan with dedicated outreach, mentorship programs for women entrepreneurs, and performance‑based incentives for VC funds.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 49 – Goal of at least 30 % women‑owned/led beneficiaries; current 26 % women‑led.

gen_risks.description: The existing grievance mechanism may not be accessible to all stakeholders, leading to unresolved complaints.
gen_risks.mitigation: Upgrade GM procedures, add multilingual channels, train staff on handling complaints, and publish quarterly grievance reports.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 82 – GM system requires enhancement to ensure accessibility.

gen_risks.description: Procurement processes could face delays or non‑compliance due to under‑developed tools and templates.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint a qualified procurement specialist, adopt standard World Bank procurement documents, and conduct annual ex‑post reviews.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 74 – Procurement risk rated Moderate; tools under development.

gen_risks.description: Exchange‑rate fluctuations between USD (loan currency) and JOD (local expenditures) could affect project budgeting.
gen_risks.mitigation: Use forward‑exchange contracts or currency hedges and maintain a contingency buffer in the budget.
gen_risks.evidence: Datasheet – Currency equivalents JOD 0.709 = $US1; disbursements in USD (Section 69).

gen_risks.description: Delays in World Bank disbursements or IFR approvals could postpone investment commitments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare IFRs ahead of schedule, assign a dedicated liaison officer with MOPIC, and monitor disbursement timelines weekly.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 70 – Disbursement based on quarterly IFRs submitted within 45 days.

gen_risks.description: Jordanian labor law gaps relative to ESS2 (e.g., non‑discrimination) may expose the project to compliance issues.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement gap‑filling measures outlined in the ESCP, conduct regular labor‑law compliance audits, and train employers on non‑discrimination policies.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 80 – Identified gaps with ESS2 and added gap‑filling measures.

gen_risks.description: Overlap of exposure to the same startup through both Fund‑of‑Funds and co‑investment components could amplify loss.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain a centralized exposure register, set a maximum aggregate exposure per startup (e.g., 10 % of total capital), and require independent review before additional investment.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 36 – Risks related to total exposure to the same startups through both components.

gen_risks.description: Geopolitical volatility in the region may deter foreign investors and affect capital inflows.
gen_risks.mitigation: Broaden the investor base to include regional sovereign wealth funds, obtain political‑risk insurance, and highlight Jordan’s stable macro‑economic reforms in marketing materials.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 1 – Jordan faces vulnerabilities tied to its position in a geopolitically volatile region.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is rated Substantial. External economic shocks, regional instability and related uncertainties, or a downturn in global venture capital markets could reduce investor confidence and slow private capital mobilization. Additionally, Jordan's nascent venture capital market and competition from more developed ecosystems in neighboring countries may impact startup retention and funding.

Other risks are rated Substantial and relate to geopolitical risk. Jordan's strategic location makes it susceptible to a complex set of geopolitical challenges that have intensified in recent years, due to the current Conflict in the Middle East and its repercussions for investment, trade, and tourism in the region. Increasing geopolitical risks may prompt adjustments in policy and budgetary priorities and/or contribute to delays in implementation.
gt_risks.mitigation: By combining regional and global diplomacy, building international partnerships, staying the course on political and economic modernization reforms, implementing prudent fiscal policies, and strategic security measures, Jordan has maintained its resilience and stability despite continuous crises.
